title: Weekly arXiv research digest
description: An agent pulls new papers matching your keywords each week, summarizes each in 3 bullets, and flags the few worth reading in full.
steps: List 5–10 keywords and arXiv categories you follow.
Have the agent query the arXiv API for papers from the last 7 days.
Ask for a 3-bullet summary per paper plus a 'why it matters to me' line based on your stated interests.
Rank and keep the top 10; send as one email digest.
Each week, mark which picks were useful and add that feedback to the prompt.

title: Customer interview synthesizer
description: Turns a batch of interview transcripts into recurring themes, direct quotes, and open questions, with every claim linked to a transcript.
steps: Export transcripts as text files (one per interview).
Ask the agent to extract pains, jobs-to-be-done, and objections per interview, with verbatim quotes.
Have it cluster findings across interviews and count how many interviews mention each theme.
Require a transcript reference for every quote so you can verify.
Review and edit the themes doc before sharing it with the team.

title: Support macro drafter from resolved tickets
description: Reads your last month of solved tickets, finds the most repeated questions, and drafts reusable reply macros for a human to approve.
steps: Export ~200 recently solved tickets (question + final agent reply).
Ask the agent to group them by intent and rank groups by volume.
For the top 10 intents, draft a macro using your best-performing past replies as the source.
Have a support lead review tone and policy accuracy before publishing.
Repeat monthly and retire macros that are no longer used.

title: Support ticket triage and tagging
description: Classifies each incoming ticket by topic, urgency, and sentiment, and routes it to the right queue with a suggested first reply.
steps: Define a short tag list and urgency rules (e.g. outage, billing, how-to).
Trigger the agent on every new ticket via Zapier or a webhook.
Have it return JSON: tag, urgency, sentiment, suggested reply.
Apply tags automatically; keep replies as internal notes until accuracy is proven.
Spot-check 20 tickets a week and refine the rules.

title: Blog post drafts from a rough outline
description: Expands your bullet outline into a first draft in your voice, using your past posts as style references, while leaving facts for you to check.
steps: Paste 2–3 of your past posts as style samples.
Give the agent a bullet outline and the target reader.
Ask for a draft that marks every factual claim with [CHECK].
Edit the draft yourself; verify each [CHECK] item.
Ask for 5 title options and a meta description at the end.

title: Podcast show notes and chapters
description: Takes an episode transcript and produces show notes, timestamped chapters, and a short list of pull quotes.
steps: Transcribe the episode with timestamps (Whisper or your host's transcript).
Ask the agent for a 100-word summary, 5–8 chapters with timestamps, and 3 pull quotes.
Check timestamps against the audio.
Paste into your podcast host and episode page.

title: Weekly metrics report writer
description: Pulls numbers from your dashboards each Monday and writes a short plain-English report of what changed and what to look into.
steps: Keep your key metrics in one sheet with a row per week.
Schedule the agent to read the latest two weeks every Monday.
Ask for: biggest changes, possible causes to investigate, and nothing speculative stated as fact.
Post the draft to a private Slack channel for review before sharing.

title: Weekly meal plan and grocery list
description: Plans a week of dinners around your diet, budget, and what's already in the fridge, then outputs a grocery list grouped by store aisle.
steps: Tell the agent household size, dietary limits, budget, and cooking time per night.
List what's already in your fridge and pantry.
Ask for 5 dinners that reuse ingredients, plus a grocery list grouped by aisle.
Save as a checklist in your notes app; tweak and reuse winning weeks.

title: Vendor contract first-pass reviewer
description: Reads a vendor contract and lists renewal terms, notice periods, liability caps, and unusual clauses so you know what to ask a lawyer.
steps: Upload the contract PDF.
Ask for a table: term, auto-renewal, notice period, price changes, liability, data handling, termination.
Ask it to quote the exact clause for each item.
Flag anything unusual; get legal review for anything that matters. This is not legal advice.

title: Test writer for untested legacy code
description: An agent reads an untested module, writes characterization tests that lock in current behavior, and runs them until they pass.
steps: Pick one module with no tests.
Ask the agent to write tests describing what the code does today, not what it should do.
Have it run the test suite and fix the tests (not the code) until green.
Review the tests, commit them, then refactor with a safety net.

title: Dependency upgrade agent
description: Upgrades one outdated dependency at a time, reads the changelog, fixes breaking changes, and opens a PR per upgrade.
steps: Run `npm outdated` (or your package manager's equivalent).
Ask the agent to upgrade one package, read its changelog, and fix breakages.
Require the build and tests to pass before it opens a PR.
Review and merge one PR at a time.

title: Codebase onboarding guide generator
description: Explores a repo and writes a guide for new contributors: architecture, where things live, how to run it, and common gotchas.
steps: Open the repo in your agent and ask for a tour of the top-level structure.
Ask it to trace one real request or feature end to end.
Have it write ONBOARDING.md with setup steps it actually ran.
Ask a new teammate to follow it and fix what's wrong.

title: Lead list enricher
description: Takes a CSV of company names and adds website, what they do, and a one-line personalization hook from public pages, marking anything it couldn't find.
steps: Prepare a CSV of company names (and domains if you have them).
Ask the agent to browse each company's site and fill in: description, size signal, recent news.
Require 'not found' instead of guesses.
Spot-check 10 rows before using the list for outreach.

title: Sales call prep brief
description: Before each sales call, writes a one-page brief on the company, the attendees' public roles, and good discovery questions.
steps: Trigger on calendar events with external attendees.
Have the agent research the company site, recent news, and attendee titles.
Ask for a one-page brief: context, likely priorities, 5 discovery questions.
Read it 10 minutes before the call.

title: Receipt and expense categorizer
description: Reads receipts forwarded to an inbox, extracts vendor, amount, date, and category, and appends them to a spreadsheet for monthly bookkeeping.
steps: Set up a label or address for forwarded receipts.
Have the agent extract vendor, date, amount, currency, and category from each.
Append rows to a sheet; flag low-confidence items for review.
Reconcile against your bank statement monthly.

title: Subscription and recurring charge audit
description: Scans a few months of bank or card statements, lists every recurring charge, and highlights duplicates and things you may have forgotten.
steps: Export 3 months of transactions as CSV from your bank.
Ask the agent to find recurring merchants and their frequency and amount.
Have it flag duplicates, price increases, and unfamiliar charges.
Cancel what you don't use yourself; the agent only makes the list.

title: Job application tailor
description: Compares your resume to a job posting, lists gaps and matching experience, and drafts a tailored cover letter you edit before sending.
steps: Paste your resume and the job description.
Ask for matched requirements, gaps, and which experience to move up.
Ask for a short cover letter using only facts from your resume.
Edit in your own voice before applying.

title: Plain-English questions to SQL
description: Lets teammates ask questions about your database in plain English; the agent writes read-only SQL, runs it, and shows both the query and the result.
steps: Create a read-only database role for the agent.
Give the agent your schema and a few example queries with explanations.
Have it always show the SQL alongside the answer.
Review wrong answers and add them as examples to the prompt.
